'''''Iberis saxatilis''''', the '''rock candytuft''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Brassicaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern [[Europe]] and northwest [[Africa]].<ref name="MBG">{{Cite web|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278055&isprofile=0&basic=iberis|title=''Iberis saxatilis''|publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder|access-date=2022-04-28}}</ref><ref name="POWO">{{Cite web|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:285650-1|title=''Iberis saxatilis''|publisher=Kew Plants of the World Online|access-date=2022-04-28}}</ref> The species is typically used as an ornamental rock and alpine garden [[perennial plant]] because of its decorative flowers and cascading growth habit.<ref name="MBG"/> ''[[Iberis]]'' is so named because many members of the genus come from the [[Iberian Peninsula]] in south west Europe.<ref name="MBG"/> The species name ''saxatilis'' means "growing among rocks," referring to the preferred substrate of this species.<ref name="MBG"/>

==Range==
The natural range for this species is [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Italy]], [[Switzerland]], the [[Balkan Peninsula]], the [[Crimean Peninsula]], and [[Morocco]].<ref name="MBG"/><ref name="POWO"/> In 2017, a new subspecies—''Iberis saxatilis'' subsp. ''magnesiana''—was identified in [[Turkey]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oskay |first1=Dilek |date= 9 May 2017 |title= A new subspecies of Iberis saxatilis (Brassicaceae) from Turkey |url=https://www.biotaxa.org/Phytotaxa/article/view/phytotaxa.306.2.5 |journal=Phytotaxa |volume=306 |issue=2 |page=153 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.306.2.5 |access-date=2022-04-28|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Description==
This species is a spreading and low-growing perennial.<ref name="MBG"/> Depending on the wintertime harshness of its environment, it may be evergreen or semi-evergreen.<ref name="MBG"/> It produces numerous snowflake-like white flowers, the petals of which take on a pink or purple tinge with age.<ref name="MBG"/> The plant is able to spread via adventitious rooting of stems that make contact with soil.<ref name="MBG"/>

==Cultivation==
Rock candytuft is typically grown in gardens that simulate the rocky alpine conditions of the plant's natural habitat.<ref name="MBG"/> It thrives and flowers best in full sun with well-drained soil, but will tolerate partial shade.<ref name="MBG"/> Poorly drained soil often causes crown rot in this species.<ref name="MBG"/>
